title: Same pipeline, new model: Claude Fable 5.2 rebuilt every Stone Age model in my city builder (Python → Blender, before/after)
author: from_makondo
selftext:
A few weeks ago I posted Agewalker here, a city builder I design while Claude Code writes all the code, including the Python scripts that generate every 3D model in Blender. The common feedback was fair: it looked like boxes.

So I had Claude Fable 5.2 redo the whole Stone Age with the same approach: no image or 3D generators, only Python that builds the mesh in Blender. 45 models: the mayor, 15 buildings, Stonehenge in 5 build stages, townsfolk, animals, trees, roads.

**What changed:**

* The mayor went from 468 to about 3,000 triangles: a wolf-fur collar, a claw necklace, a skull-topped staff. Same skeleton and pivots, so animations didn’t break.
* Before, models were mostly boxes. Now Claude wrote a small toolkit of organic shapes for Blender (lofts, sweeps, hanging hides, feathers, layered pine boughs) and builds everything from it.
* A “stage” script renders each model and runs checks (footprint, triangle budget, no two colours on one face), so Claude looks at its own result before I do.
* A regression check confirmed that the other \~450 models of the game export byte for byte as before.

**What it cost:** about 20% fps, mostly from the forest. Still far above 60 fps on my machine, but it’s measured, not guessed.

**Where I still had to step in:** the first trees came out wrong (spiky star-shaped tiers, a lumpy crown). I rejected them and they were redone. Visual judgment is still the part I can’t hand off.

This isn’t in the playtest build yet. The other five ages get the same pass one by one. Happy to answer questions about the setup.

comments.author: xens999
comments.body: I don't know why but "Mayor of the Stoneage" just makes me laugh. As a codex user i'm also jealous of your new model congrats.

replies.author: xens999
replies.body: Just the hassle of all my chats being on the one, I'll wait probably until 6.2 is out then make a decision seems like openai is falling behind a lot at the moment.

comments.author: Kepler___
comments.body: This looks modeled on native Americans more than the Bell-Breaker people (I'm taking your mention of \*the\* Stonehenge literally here, as opposed to \*a\* stonehenge) the AI is probably just referencing generic pre-metal working societies. Have Fable look into what we know about them and redo the design based on that, inconsistences like this are what actually make AI art stand out the most, there's no real thought in any design choice beyond vague pattern matching. The more you can sculpt these specifics the better, and archeological research can actually do a lot of this heavy lifting for you.

replies.author: from_makondo
replies.body: This is genuinely useful, and you’re right: tipis and a feathered headdress are Plains peoples, not Neolithic Britain. The Stone Age is meant to be a general one, but with Stonehenge in it that doesn’t hold up. I’ll have it look into what’s known about Neolithic and Bell Beaker houses and clothing and rethink the designs.

comments.author: Putrid_Clue_2127
comments.body: While I absolutely love fable 5.2 so far, this is not really an accurate representation of the model differences. You could have easily achieved the after model in opus 5.5

comments.author: TopTippityTop
comments.body: Use a different pipeline with tripo, or some other 3d generative solution, unless you want your game to look like low value AI prototype aesthetics.

replies.author: from_makondo
replies.body: Thanks. I chose models as code on purpose: one palette, fixed triangle budgets, and I can change all 45 at once. But fair, if it keeps reading as a prototype, I’ll reconsider.

comments.author: OneMoreFightGame
comments.body: It's incredible how detailed Fable is. I don't know much about triangles and blender and all that, but the added details are awesome and I'm sure you're absolutely stoked for how good the upgraded look is
